leon: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's trunk merge I see p99 token latency +12% on the paged-attn + bf16 + interleaved-KV path. Profiling attached (very rough).

maya: ugh, can you paste the perf summary here?

leon: sure, truncated output from perf-runner:
```
seq=1024 dtype=bf16 layout=interleaved kernel=paged-attn
throughput: 320 tok/s (prev 360)
avg_latency/token: 2.8ms (prev 2.4ms)
p99_latency/token: 18.6ms (prev 16.6ms)
KV hit ratio: 0.74 -> 0.59
warp_miss_rate: 0.12 -> 0.19
```

sam: interesting that KV hit ratio dropped. Is batching different? any change to continuous batching heuristics?

leon: we didn't change batching config in this deploy. Selector logs show paged-attn still chosen for seq>768 and when layout==interleaved. snippet:  `kernel_selector: choose paged_attn (est_cost 12.3ms) over fused (est_cost 13.1ms)`

zara: my hypothesis: bf16 packing + interleaved stride produced unaligned KV base offsets leading to bank conflicts on the paged kernel. we've seen similar when stride % 64 != 0.

ryan: could also be cacheline fragmentation. On some GPUs, bf16 uses 2 bytes per element so interleaving can create 48-byte strides which are bad for our fused/paged banking.

maya: can we repro with a microbench sweeping stride and dtype? we should test interleaved vs separate KV layout and also float16 vs bf16.

perf-bot: perf-alert: paged-attn p99 increase detected for model/llama-13b on env=staging; delta +12% (auto-tag: kv-layout-regression)

sam: also check batching heuristics — if effective batch size changed, it can alter kernel choice boundary because kernel cost function depends on batch*seq. maybe continuous batching aggregated more prefixes so paged path had worse locality.

leon: I captured continuous-batcher stats around the regression window: `avg_batch_tokens` went from 710->920 for the affected model, likely due to increased concurrency. That pushes selector more often into paged region.

zara: plan: 1) microbench sweep (dtype float16/bf16, layout interleaved/separate, strides [32,48,64,96]) 2) run canary toggling selector to prefer fused for batch_token < 1k 3) enable extra KV alignment padding in interleaved layout (+16 bytes) to see if warp_miss_rate drops 4) metricized canary on p99 tokens and KV hit ratio.

maya: I'll run the microbench and canary tomorrow morning. canary flags to use: `--kernel-preference=fused:threshold=1000` and `--kv-align-pad=16` (will push through canary infra).

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/kv-layout-fallback -> staging at 2024-11-07T09:00Z (initiator: maya).

ryan: add a small synthetic that simulates cold KV population + interleaved access pattern so we get realistic early-request behavior. Also log `warp_miss_rate` per bank.

leon: thanks — for follow-ups: if microbench shows alignment fix helps, we can add an alignment pad in runtime as an opt-in flag and then evaluate cost trade-offs. If not, fallback to separate-KV layout for bf16 when seq>768.

maya: noted. I'll post results in this thread. :thumbsup: :eyes:
